title: WS Trail History – Western States 100
claims: The official trail description divides the trail into six sections.
Section One climbs more than 2,500 ft in its first four miles, crests at Emigrant Pass at 8,750 ft, passes through the Granite Chief Wilderness and averages 7,000 ft in altitude.
In many years Section One is covered entirely in snow.
Leaving Robinson Flat the trail climbs to Little Bald Mountain and then descends 1,043 ft to Miller's Defeat.
Last Chance is a mining ghost town that marks the jumping-off point for the canyons.
The first canyon, Deadwood, drops about 2,000 ft and then climbs an extremely steep 1,500 ft to Devil's Thumb.
The second canyon, El Dorado, has a descent of 2,600 ft followed by an 1,800 ft climb to Michigan Bluff.
The most rugged 13 miles between Last Chance and Michigan Bluff is listed in the National Register of Historic Places.
Runners may encounter temperatures as high as 110 degrees F (43 degrees C) while traversing the canyons.
From Michigan Bluff the trail dips in and out of Volcano Canyon before reaching pavement for the first time on the outskirts of Foresthill.
From Foresthill the California Trail is a 16-mile rolling descent to the bottom of the American River Canyon.
Rucky Chucky crosses the American River just below a class 6 rapids; water flow is reduced when possible, a cable runs bank to bank and boats are used in high-water years.

From Rucky Chucky the trail climbs to Green Gate, follows undulating terrain through Auburn Lake Trails and Brown's Bar, drops to the river again and climbs to the Cool limestone quarry where it crosses Highway 49 less than seven miles from the finish.
No Hands Bridge, officially the Mountain Quarries Bridge, was the longest concrete-arch bridge in the world at the time of its construction and is listed in the National Register of Historic Places.
No Hands Bridge is the lowest point on the entire trail, after which the trail climbs to Robie Point and the outskirts of Auburn.
At Robie Point runners are 1.3 miles from the finish at Placer High School stadium.
Runners step onto pavement for the third and last time in 100 miles at Robie Point.
